extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their advisors (corporate counsel, accountants, auditors, and investors)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and implementation guidance for public-company climate-related disclosures (Regulation S-K/Subpart 1500 and limited Regulation S-X amendments), including what must be disclosed in financial statements, materiality/attribution standards, exemptions, tagging, and assurance standards. Focuses on compliance scope, thresholds, cost considerations, and phased implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of financial statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules focus financial statement disclosures on expenditures related to severe weather events and other natural conditions and the purchase and use of carbon offsets and RECs (one type of transition activity), rather than requiring disclosures for transition activities generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrower scope responds to commenter concerns about feasibility; discrete expenditures of this type are typically captured in books and records and are therefore feasible to disclose. The final rules do not require disclosure of expenditures generally related to transition activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1% disclosure threshold (aggregate application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1% disclosure threshold will be applied only to two aggregate amounts: (1) the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses (if equal to or exceeds one percent of the absolute value of income or loss before income tax expense or benefit); and/or (2) the aggregate amount of the absolute value of capitalized costs and charges (if equal to or exceeds one percent of the absolute value of stockholders' equity or deficit), subject to de minimis thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the proposed requirement to apply the 1% threshold on a line-by-line basis throughout financial statements, substantially reducing burden. The thresholds determine whether disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution principle — 'significant contributing factor'
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules prescribe an attribution principle requiring registrants to use a 'significant contributing factor' standard to attribute expenditures, costs, and losses to severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses commenters' concerns about isolating and attributing expenditures by allowing a significant contributing factor standard rather than demanding perfect isolation or line-by-line attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offsets/RECs disclosure conditional on materiality to targets/goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose costs, expenditures, and losses incurred in connection with the purchase and use of carbon offsets and RECs only if carbon offsets or RECs have been used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is narrower than the proposed rule (which would have required disclosure of expenditures to reduce GHGs or mitigate transition risks more generally) and limits disclosure to situations where offsets/RECs materially support disclosed targets/goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of estimates and assumptions limited to materially impacted items
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules limit the scope of the requirement to disclose estimates and assumptions in the financial statements to only those estimates and assumptions materially impacted by severe weather events and natural conditions and any climate-related targets or transition plans disclosed by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the proposal, registrants would have been required to disclose estimates and assumptions impacted by transition activities more broadly; the final rule narrows that to materially impacted items to reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical fiscal year disclosure — prospective-only limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure for historical fiscal year(s) is required only to the extent the required information was previously disclosed or required to be disclosed (i.e., the rule is prospective and does not require registrants to retroactively estimate historical data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change responds to commenter concerns that retroactive estimation would be burdensome and costly; under the final rules, registrants are not required to provide disclosure for fiscal periods in which they were not required to collect or report the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRCs and EGCs accommodations and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs) are exempt from the GHG emissions disclosure requirement and the accompanying assurance requirement, and are provided extended phased-in compliance periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These accommodations are intended to mitigate disproportionate burdens on smaller registrants, allowing more time to observe market practices and prepare for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable Inline XBRL tagging requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures required by the final rules must be filed in a machine-readable data language (Inline XBRL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging is expected to improve comparability, reduce investors' costs of acquiring and processing information, facilitate data analysis, and reduce informational advantages of informed traders; it supports standardized, machine-readable data for investors and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted assurance standard (ISO 14064-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules permit assurance providers to use the ISO 14064-3 attestation standard for GHG emissions assurance engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing ISO 14064-3 should limit circumstances where registrants must seek different attestation engagements and reduce burdens related to assurance provider availability and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualifier for risk management disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk management disclosure is required only with respect to climate risks that are material to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This materiality qualifier reduces the scope of mandatory disclosures to risks that meaningfully affect the company, addressing concerns about managerial attention diversion and overbroad disclosure of non-material issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary activities trigger disclosure only after materiality determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require registrants to undertake scenario analysis, targets, or goals; if a registrant voluntarily does so, the related disclosures (and costs) are required only following a materiality determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants that voluntarily conduct scenario analysis or set targets will incur disclosure obligations only if those items are material, which reduces mandatory burdens and avoids penalizing voluntary preparatory activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to disclose impacts to cash flows, revenues, or cost savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants will not be required to disclose any impacts to the Statement of Cash Flows, nor will they be required to disclose impacts to revenues, cost savings, or cost reductions under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responds to commenters who noted such amounts are often not captured in a registrant's books and records and would be particularly difficult to disclose; it substantially reduces compliance burden compared to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC cost-estimation methodology and upper-bound figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC reviewed commenter cost estimates, adjusted them to reflect changes in the final rules (which substantially reduce burdens), and used staff knowledge of accounting practices to set illustrative upper-bound estimates (e.g., $500,000 initial direct cost upper bound; ongoing costs up to 75% of initial; incremental audit fees upper bound $23,000 per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff considered commenter-provided estimates (often in the millions), but adjusted downward given the elimination of primary cost drivers from the proposal. These figures are treated as upper bounds and will vary by registrant size and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing direct compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance costs depend on registrant-specific factors: whether the registrant already discloses Scope 1/2 emissions or uses TCFD/CDP frameworks, industry (e.g., insurance companies with complex exposures), registrant size and complexity, frequency of exposure to severe weather events, and availability of third-party service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants already aligned with TCFD or subject to similar state laws may face lower incremental costs; smaller registrants may face proportionally higher fixed costs; markets and increased supplier competition are expected to reduce costs over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation of competitive harm and scope exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules remove several prescriptive elements from the proposal, add materiality qualifiers, and limit certain applications (e.g., do not apply to private companies in certain business combination filings) to reduce the risk of disclosing competitively sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes are intended to balance investor informational benefits and registrant competitive concerns; the narrower requirements and materiality qualifiers limit circumstances requiring disclosure of sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased implementation to mitigate short-term market constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules provide phased-in compliance periods (including extended phases for smaller registrants) to give the market time to supply needed third-party services and assurance providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased implementation is expected to mitigate short-term increases in consultant/assurance costs and allow new providers to enter the market, which over time should lower service fees and improve availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose locations of properties/operations subject to material physical risks (Item 1502(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure of the location of company properties or operations that are subject to material physical risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This location disclosure is intended to help investors assess exposure to physical risks; registrants should be aware this could influence managerial decisions (e.g., relocation) and might have competitive or operational consequences.
